transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-05-09 | Time: 09:30 PT | Duration: ~54m | Attendees: Sofia M, Devon P (Redwood); Aisha K, Tom R, Maya P, Liam O (Northwood)

Summary: Quick kickoff to get the implementation ball rolling for Northwood's pilot. Agree on data flow, VPC peering, benchmark plan, and deliverables.

Questions: who is the network owner, what are the SLA expectations for the pilot, do we need on-prem package?

[00:00] Sofia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros — I'm Sofia, AE, Devon from solutions will do the technical bits. Aisha, want to kick us off with goals?

[00:18] Aisha (VP Eng): Yeah thanks. Um, main thing is we want to validate latency and cost for our question-answering product. We plan to go live with a limited pilot for a subset of customers in Q3. So main things: secure network connectivity, predictable latency, and tight cost control.

[00:37] Devon (SE): Great. Quick check — what's your current infra? Maya?

[00:42] Maya (Cloud Architect): We're on AWS, EKS for inference glue, S3 for artifacts. We have private subnets and strict egress rules. We'll need VPC peering or transit gateway. Also our security team will require audit logs and KMS integration.

[01:05] Devon: Got it. Redwood supports VPC peering for Private deployments; for Hosted we can do private link too. For Dedicated, you get reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput. There's some network setup differences.

[01:25] Liam (PM): Can you say a bit more about Dedicated vs Hosted? Cost tradeoffs?

[01:30] Sofia: Sure. Hosted is fastest to get started; pay-as-you-go. Dedicated gives you committed capacity and lower per-token cost at scale, plus data isolation. Private (VPC) gives full control for compliance. For pilot, most teams start Hosted or Dedicated light and then move to Private if required.

[01:58] Tom (Head of ML): We're sensitive to tail latency. Any notes on batching and KV cache? Our queries are short, but concurrency might be high.

[02:10] Devon: We use dynamic batching and prefix/KV caching to cut per-token time for repeat contexts. For short queries, batching helps throughput but might add latency. We can tune continuous batching window, and we support low-latency SLOs with smaller batch sizes. Also quantization profiles can reduce memory and cost but may affect quality.

[02:44] Aisha: Hm, quality tradeoffs are non-negotiable for our SLAs. We can't regress.

[02:50] Devon: Understood — Redwood Optimize suggests quantization only after we run evals on your prompt set; we can pin model versions and roll out canary evaluates so you won't get regressions unexpectedly.

[03:10] Maya: For the VPC peers, do you need us to open anything other than egress to Redwood's IPs? Our security team is strict.

[03:17] Devon: Typically we ask for NAT egress to Redwood endpoints, and for Private deployments we do a peered VPC. We'll send a network diagram and a minimal firewall rule set — should be in the onboarding runbook.

[03:38] Sofia: We'll attach the runbook and a sample CloudFormation/TF snippet.

[03:45] Liam: About observability — how granular is token-level cost and latency breakdown? We want to attribute costs to features.

[03:53] Devon: You get token-level cost by route/model, per-request latency histogram, tracing hooks, and audit logs. We can ship a small dashboard config for Grafana and also S3 exports.

[04:12] Tom: Any gotchas on SSO/SAML and SCIM? Our security team needs SSO and RBAC mapping.

[04:19] Sofia: We support SSO via SAML, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. For Private we can integrate with your IdP during onboarding; we'll share the SSO runbook.

[04:35] Maya: KMS/HSM — we need keys in our account for encryption at rest, especially for logs.

[04:41] Devon: For Private we can plug into your KMS. Hosted supports customer-managed keys in many cases; we'll check the exact flow and include options (bring-your-own-KMS or Redwood-managed with strict controls).

[05:02] Aisha: Alright, pilot scope: what success metrics should we define? We're thinking P95 latency < 250ms for short queries, cost per 1k tokens under $X, and accuracy on our eval set no worse than baseline.

[05:18] Sofia: That sounds reasonable. We'll formalize those into the pilot success doc.

[05:28] Liam: Timeline — we want a two-week bench/pilot in mid-May and then a ramp to ~500 users in Q3.

[05:35] Devon: Ok, two-week window is doable. We'll schedule infra test during week 1 and quality/regression evals week 2.

[05:45] Maya: Regarding data retention: logs that contain PII — can you redact or we need to route them to our S3?

[05:52] Devon: We have redaction hooks and also the option to route logs to your S3 with configurable retention. For Private, logs can stay in your VPC entirely.

[06:05] Tom: Also curious about model selection. We want to try two model families, larger for complex summaries and smaller faster ones for chat. How do you manage model catalog and rollouts?

[06:14] Devon: We host a catalog of verified models; you can pin versions and create rollout policies (canary, A/B). We also have per-model performance profiles so we can recommend tradeoffs.

[06:30] Aisha: Great. Can Redwood run a short perf char to show perf/cost for our typical sequence length (~256) and concurrency ~80?

[06:38] Devon: Yes — action item: we'll run a perf benchmark with your prompt set and concurrency profile. We'll need sample prompts and expected sequence lengths.

[06:50] Sofia: I'll capture the action items and follow-ups.

[07:00] (background: brief side chatter, "yeah", "okay")

[07:22] Liam: Any enterprise requirements we should pre-emptively surface — e.g., SOC2, ISO?

[07:28] Sofia: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified, and we have ISO docs in our security packet. We'll send links. Also audit logs and retention policies are configurable.

[07:40] Maya: About network latency, are there regional endpoints? Our users are US/EU primarily.

[07:46] Devon: Yes we have regions; routing policy can pick by latency or cost. We'll recommend regional endpoints for the EU traffic to minimize latency and residency concerns.

[07:58] Aisha: Ok good. Anything around on-prem? Our legal asked if we can do air-gapped for extreme cases.

[08:06] Devon: We offer an on-prem package for regulated workloads, but that requires more lead time and a private control plane. For the pilot it's usually overkill unless required.

[08:20] Tom: Understood. For the benchmark, what metrics will you report back?

[08:25] Devon: We'll provide P50/P95/P99 latencies, throughput (tokens/s), error rates, cost per 1k tokens, and memory/VRAM footprint. Also model quality evals if you give us the prompt set.

[08:44] Aisha: Ok, I'd like the perf spreadsheet so we can present to execs.

[08:50] Sofia: We'll share the spreadsheet and a short exec one-pager.

[09:02] (timestamp jump — mid meeting, network/clarity issues noted)

[10:12] Maya: Quick thing — our security team will require that the onboarding runbook includes a list of required IAM roles and least-privilege suggestions.

[10:20] Devon: Absolutely — runbook includes IAM, peering instructions, and the minimal firewall open list.

[10:33] Liam: Are there any limitations on model context length or kv cache size we should be mindful of? We pass long conversation histories sometimes.

[10:41] Devon: We support up to several thousand tokens depending on the model; for very long contexts we use KV cache mechanisms. There are memory tradeoffs; we'll include recommended truncation and summarization patterns.

[10:58] Tom: Regarding rollouts, can we do A/B where one variant is quantized and one is not, to measure quality delta?

[11:06] Devon: Yes — you can route traffic and flag by route. We can do a canary that serves a subset quantized model and capture analytics.

[11:20] (minor crosstalk)

[11:35] Sofia: Alright I'm going to recap the agreed items so we leave with clarity.

[11:40] Sofia (recap): 1) Redwood will send onboarding runbook, SSO and SOC2 docs; 2) Customer to provide VPC details and prompt sets; 3) SE to run perf benchmark and share spreadsheet; 4) Schedule infra test in mid-May; 5) Define pilot success metrics (P95 < 250ms, cost target, quality baseline). Anything to add?

[11:58] Aisha: That covers it. One ask — can you tint the runbook with a minimal TF/CF template? saves us time.

[12:05] Devon: Yup, we'll include TF and a minimal CloudFormation snippet.

[12:12] Liam: Who's the primary contact for blockers during the pilot?

[12:16] Sofia: I'll be the AE contact and Devon the SE. We'll also add a CSM once we move from pilot to initial ramp.

[12:25] Maya: Ok we'll aim to get the VPC/CIDR and samples by Tuesday.

[12:31] (wrap-up pleasantries)

[12:40] Sofia: Thanks again. We'll follow up with the runbook and schedule the benchmark.

[12:47] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript had a few mis-heard product names (e.g., "KV cash"), and some speaker attribution swapped between "Tom" and "Speaker 2" in earlier segments. Overall medium quality; key action items verified by participants.
